segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Thank you, Mr. Chairman. And good morning to our witnesses who are testifying today. I want to thank each of you for being here to discuss a topic of grave importance to our national security. Earlier this year, a Chinese spy balloon was shot down off the coast of my home state of South Carolina. Since the Roswell incident in 1947, many Americans have wondered about the dangers of unknown objects crisscrossing our skies, whether these are UAPs or weather phenomena, advanced technology from American allied or enemy forces, or something more out of this world. So my first question, I have several questions, and if we can just be quick on these first two, I’m going to ask each of you the same question, and then I’ll get to each of you individually. The first one. When you reported your experiences with a UAP, did MVU face any repercussions with your superiors? Yes or no?

segments.speaker: GravesRyan
segments.text: No.

segments.speaker: FravorDavid
segments.text: No!

segments.speaker: GruschDavid
segments.text: I’ve actually never seen anything personally, believe it or not.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: All right. And then do you believe there’s an active disinformation campaign within our government to deny existence of UAPs? Yes or no?

segments.speaker: GravesRyan
segments.text: I don’t have an answer to that.

segments.speaker: GruschDavid
segments.text: As previously stated publicly, yes.

segments.speaker: FravorDavid
segments.text: I think. Previously. With, like, project Blue Book. Yes, but currently I don’t speak for the United States government.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Okay, thank you. I have a few questions for Mr. Graves. What percentage of UAP sightings, in your belief, go unreported by our pilots?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: This is an approximation based off of my personal experience speaking with a number of pilots, but I would estimate we’re somewhere near 5% reporting, perhaps.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: So like 95% basically don’t report seeing UAPs.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: That’s just my personal estimate.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: In the incident off Virginia Beach, do you believe the Navy took the danger to your aircraft seriously after it was reported?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Absolutely.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: A few questions for Mr. Favor. As an expert naval aviator, have you ever seen an object that looked and moved like the Tic TAC UAP?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: No.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Did the Tic TAC UAP move in such a way that defied the laws of physics ?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: The way we understand them, yes.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Many dismiss UAP reports as classified weapons testing by our own government. But in your experience as a pilot, does our government typically test advanced weapon systems right next to multimillion dollar jets without informing our pilots?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: No, we have test ranges for that.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: It took over 15 years for your encounter with the Tic TAC to be declassified. Do you feel there was a good reason to prevent lawmakers from having access to this footage?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: No, I just think it was ignored when it happened and it just sat somewhere in a file, never got reported in a drawer.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: It happens a lot up here. Shocker. Mr. Grusch, a couple of questions for you too, sir, this morning, what percentage of UAPs do you feel are adequately investigated by the US government? Of the 5% that are reported.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I can only speak for my personal leadership over at Nga. I tried to look at every report that came through that I could triage.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Do you believe that officials at the highest levels of our national security apparatus have unlawfully withheld information from Congress and subverted our oversight authority?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: There are certain elected leaders that had more information that I’m not sure what they’ve shared with certain gang of eight members or et cetera, but certainly I would not be surprised.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Okay. You’ve stated that the government is in possession of potentially non-human spacecraft. Based on your experience and extensive conversations with experts, do you believe our government has made contact with intelligent extraterrestrials?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Something I can’t discuss in public setting.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Okay. I can’t ask when you think this occurred (laughs), if you believe we have crashed craft stated earlier, do we have the bodies of the pilots who piloted this craft?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: As I’ve stated publicly already in my News Nation interview, biologics came with some of these recoveries. Yeah.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Were they, I guess, human or non-human?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Biologics non-human. And that was the assessment of people with direct knowledge on the program I talked to that are currently still on the program.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: And was this documentary evidence as video, photos, eyewitness? Like, how would that be determined?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: The specific documentation I would have to talk to you in a <abbr title="Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility">SCIF</abbr> about got you.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Okay. And you may or may not be able to answer my last question, and maybe we get into a <abbr title="Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility">SCIF</abbr> at the next hearing that we have. But who in the government either what agency subagency, what contractors, who should be called into the next hearing about UAPs, either in a public setting or even in a private setting. And you probably can’t name names, but what agencies or organizations, contractors, et cetera, do we need to call in to get these questions answered? Whether it’s about funding, what programs are happening, and what’s out there.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I can give you a specific, cooperative and hostile witness list of specific individuals that were in those.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: And how soon can we get that list?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I’m happy to provide that to you after the hearing.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Super. Thank you. And I yield back.
